europe_wide_onset.endpoint: time to first classified downstream-migration crossing

external_barrier_evidence.source: Huisman et al. 2023 Journal of Fish Biology DOI 10.1111/jfb.15398
external_barrier_evidence.endpoint: number of missed sluicing events before passage
external_barrier_evidence.note: Paper also reports higher weight -> more missed events; source authors discuss stimulus-threshold and asset-protection explanations. Published IRR interval and Wald p are not numerically concordant, so use the direction as contextual evidence rather than a precise pooled effect.

external_barrier_evidence.source: van Rijn et al. 2026 Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences DOI 10.1139/cjfas-2025-0359
external_barrier_evidence.endpoint: number of missed passage opportunities before passage
external_barrier_evidence.note: Source authors connect the result to stronger flow thresholds or greater risk aversion. Published IRR interval and Wald p are not numerically concordant, so use the direction as contextual evidence rather than a precise pooled effect.

external_barrier_evidence.source: van der Knaap et al. 2025 Movement Ecology DOI 10.1186/s40462-025-00588-9
external_barrier_evidence.note: This is activity, not passage delay; it is a mechanistic boundary consistent with greater selectivity/lower routine activity in better-conditioned eels.

synthesis.observed_pattern: Better capture body state predicts stronger/earlier migration activation in the Europe-wide cohort, yet better condition is associated with greater delay/selectivity at engineered passage barriers in two independent Dutch systems.
synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The behavioral effect of body state changes sign across migration phases: reserves/readiness facilitate entry into migration, but once a risky or restrictive barrier is encountered, high-condition individuals can afford to wait for stronger/safer opportunities and therefore show greater passage selectivity.
not_claimed: the same condition metric was measured identically across datasets
body condition causally determines either activation or barrier delay
all barriers should produce the reversal

decisive_tests: Dutch 2026 arrival-defined risk set: condition x discharge-opportunity strength after direct barrier arrival
test condition effect on passage timing in a permeable/natural route where anthropogenic risk is weak
within-individual repeated body-state or independent physiological reserve measurement
